title: Electrolyte Coffee Explained: Caffeine, Minerals and Hydration
summary: Electrolyte Coffee adds sodium, potassium and calcium to your cup in an instant coconut water Americano, ready anytime. Learn how it handles hydration and caffeine.
body_markdown:
You have twenty minutes between waking up and the first mile. You want that hit of caffeine, but you also want electrolytes before the sweat you're about to put in. One cup that covers both? It's not too good to be true: It’s called[Electrolyte Coffee](https://lairdsuperfood.com/collections/electrolyte-coffee) and it's delicious enough that you'll want to start every day with it.


Each glass blends iced coffee energy with sports drink hydration in one simple, easy-to-use mix. It's deliciously bold, slightly sweet, and thoroughly refreshing, all with 0 g added sugar. To live up to its name, every serving provides a good source of sodium, potassium and calcium, with a moderate 55 mg of caffeine.


## What Is Electrolyte Coffee?


Electrolyte Coffee is the iced coconut water Americano you may already know, now as an instant mix. To enjoy a glass any time of day, simply stir or shake a serving into cold water and pour it over ice. No need for a fancy espresso maker or a trip to see your favorite barista — this shelf-stable mix is ready in seconds whenever you are.


Inside each cup is a foundation of organic Arabica instant coffee and coconut water powder. Sea salt and a bioactive multi-mineral complex bring the numbers to 220 mg of sodium, 440 mg of potassium and 160 mg of calcium. A touch of monk fruit provides natural sweetness to all three flavors with 0g added sugar, and the vanilla and orange flavors come from real food.


## How Electrolyte Coffee Works


Electrolytes are minerals like sodium, potassium, magnesium and calcium that help your body manage hydration and fluid balance. You lose water and sodium in sweat, so a hot day or a long, sweaty session raises what you need. Highly active people may benefit from more sodium, in particular, to offset those sweat losses. The everyday advice is simple: keep sipping fluids all day, and drink more minerals when it's hot or you're sweating hard.


### What Each Electrolyte Does


Our Electrolyte Coffee gets its sodium from sea salt, its potassium from coconut water powder and its calcium from a bioactive multi-mineral complex sourced from the sea. Each serving supplies a good source (10% DV) of all three.


These minerals, plus magnesium, each do specific jobs in your nerves and muscles.


-


**Sodium:** Sodium is the main mineral in the fluid outside your cells, and it helps hold that fluid volume steady. It also helps your[nerves and muscles work properly](https://medlineplus.gov/sodium.html) . The Daily Value is 2,300 mg.


-


**Potassium:** Your body needs potassium for normal[kidney and heart function, muscle contraction and nerve transmission](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Potassium-Consumer) . The Daily Value is 4,700 mg.


-


**Magnesium:** Magnesium is a helper for more than 300 enzyme systems, including those behind muscle and nerve function. It also helps[move calcium and potassium across cell membranes](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/magnesium-HealthProfessional?rf=32471) , which matters for normal nerve signals and heart rhythm. The Daily Value is 420 mg.


-


**Calcium:** Most calcium sits in bones and teeth. A small circulating pool helps[muscles contract, nerves signal and blood vessels tighten and relax](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional) . The Daily Value is 1,300 mg.


Think of sodium and potassium as the two sides of a battery that fires each nerve signal and muscle twitch. Magnesium and calcium help keep that circuit running smoothly.


## When to Grab an Electrolyte Coffee


Runners, hikers and anyone with a full day ahead: Electrolyte Coffee fits the moments when a hot mug doesn't, and replenishes you with hydration and electrolytes you'll be glad to have later. Simply stir one stick into 8–12 oz of cold water, pour it over ice, and you're set. There's no second product to mix and no sweetener or creamer required. You get 55 mg of caffeine, natural sweetness, and real hydration in one easy, delicious glass.


Choose from Original, Vanilla or Orange — the surprising coffee pairing you didn’t know you loved. Keep a bag on hand in your pantry or desk drawer, or grab a box of single serve sticks as a travel companion anytime you’re on the move.

## How to Make Your Iced Electrolyte Coffee


1.


Pour 8–12 oz of cold water into a glass or shaker bottle.


2.


Add one stick pack or 1 1/2 tablespoons of Electrolyte Coffee.


3.


Stir or shake until mixed.


4.


Pour over ice.


Expect a bold cup of coffee with a light sweetness, served cold over ice.

## FAQ


Quick answers about our Electrolyte Coffee.


### How do you make Electrolyte Coffee?


Everything's already in the mix. Stir one stick or 1 1/2 tablespoons into 8–12 oz of cold water, then pour it over ice.


### Does Electrolyte Coffee taste salty?


Not particularly. Sea salt is there for dialed in sodium, and it smoothly complements the light sweetness of the coconut water powder without a salty taste. The cup tastes like bold iced coffee with light sweetness. The Orange and Vanilla flavors come from real orange and vanilla.


### Is Electrolyte Coffee good for runners?


Our Electrolyte Coffee makes an easy cold cup before you head out for a run. Each serving brings 55 mg of caffeine and a good source of sodium, potassium and calcium. The single-serve sticks travel with you wherever the day goes. On long or hot runs, keep drinking fluids along the way.


### How is it different from adding salt to coffee?


Plain salt in coffee misses what coconut water and our bioactive multi-mineral complex bring: potassium and other electrolytes, plus a light, natural sweetness and optional real food flavor. With Electrolyte Coffee, there's nothing to measure and no second product to mix.


### How much can you drink a day?


The FDA cites 400 mg of caffeine a day for most adults. Count sodium against your daily total of under 2,300 mg for most people. Three servings come to 165 mg of caffeine and add 660 mg of sodium. If you're pregnant or have a health condition, check with your doctor.


### Is there a decaf version?


We don't make a decaf version of Electrolyte Coffee. Each serving has 55 mg of caffeine, a little over half the roughly 96 mg in a typical brewed 8-oz cup.
